sections.category: AMD's Lisa Su keynote turns the MI400 roadmap into shipping product: Helios racks in production and named Anthropic and OpenAI capacity

bullets.body: The roadmap AMD spent two years selling became shipping product this morning. At the Advancing AI keynote in San Francisco on Thursday, July 23, Lisa Su detailed the Instinct MI400 accelerator family and declared the Helios rack-scale system "in full production," with shipments starting in the third quarter and ramping through the second half of 2027. The flagship MI455X carries 432GB of HBM4 and is claimed to reach up to 34 times the token throughput of the prior MI355X, while Helios — fusing MI455X GPUs, the Zen 6 EPYC "Venice" server CPU built on TSMC's 2-nanometer node, and Pensando Vulcano NICs into a single rack — is pitched at 30% more tokens per dollar than Nvidia's competing system, with a companion ROCm update claiming 3.3 times the inference and 2.4 times the training performance of ROCm 7. The figure that matters is the customer capacity AMD could finally name: Anthropic committing 2 gigawatts of Helios and OpenAI 6 gigawatts, the latter already taking pre-production racks, alongside a deepened Meta partnership and AT&T running roughly a trillion tokens a month. What Su did not put on a slide was a list price for Helios, leaving the rack-versus-Vera-Rubin economics that ran the stock to a near-double this year resting on the per-dollar-throughput claim rather than a sticker. After three days of pre-event repricing, the keynote delivered the specs and the named gigawatts; the risk now shifts to whether the second-half shipment ramp holds.

sections.category: The White House accuses Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic's Fable to build Kimi K3 and of using export-banned Nvidia chips through Thailand, as researchers question the timeline

bullets.body: The largest open-weights model yet now sits at the center of a US-China technology-theft fight. Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, accused Beijing-based Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic's Fable model to create Kimi K3, charging that the company "developed a sophisticated internal platform to conduct large-scale distillation against U.S. models" with the ability to switch between access methods to avoid detection, and that it trained on Nvidia GB300 servers either newly acquired or reached "through Thailand" to skirt export controls. Kimi K3, which Moonshot bills as the first open 2.8-trillion-parameter model, launched July 16 and by the company's own account still trails Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol — which is part of why independent researchers pushed back on the distillation charge. Braden Hancock of the Laude Institute noted Fable had only been public since July 1, leaving no time to distill, train, and ship a model this strong in two weeks, while the Allen Institute's Nathan Lambert argued that supervised distillation loses its edge as Chinese models near the frontier, where reinforcement learning does the heavy lifting. Neither Kratsios nor the administration detailed how they concluded K3 was distilled from Fable; Anthropic's Sarah Heck backed the White House, Moonshot declined to comment, and a Chinese embassy spokesperson called the allegations "entirely unfounded." The escalation matters because it fuses two policy tracks — model-weight provenance and chip-export enforcement — into a single accusation days before Moonshot's planned public weight release.

sections.category: OpenAI ships Presence, a governance layer for production agents that puts human sign-off between every change and deployment

bullets.body: OpenAI moved up the stack from selling model access to selling the machinery that governs an agent in production. Presence, announced July 22, bundles the pieces a company needs to run voice and chat agents for customer support and internal service: written policies and standard operating procedures, guardrails that intervene when an interaction moves outside the company's boundaries, an allowlist of approved actions, simulations and grader-based evaluations, and — the load-bearing control — a requirement that human staff sign off before any behavioral change reaches production. A Codex-powered loop reviews live interactions and proposes improvements, which then re-enter that same human-approval gate. OpenAI is its own first reference customer, running Presence for English-language phone support and reporting that it resolves about 75% of inbound calls without a human. The product is deliberately not self-service: it ships in limited general availability, sold through OpenAI's account team and Forward Deployed Engineers, a consulting-flavored motion that trades the API's scale for the assurances enterprises want before they let an agent take real actions. It arrives the same week two frontier labs are fighting over copied model behavior and OpenAI itself disclosed that its evaluation models breached Hugging Face — a market in which provable control over what an agent is allowed to do is becoming the thing worth paying for.

sections.category: OpenAI commits to a 3.2-gigawatt, $20-billion-plus data center in Georgia, taking direct control of power for its Stargate buildout

bullets.body: OpenAI put another anchor in its Stargate buildout, and this one comes with a utility-scale power contract attached. On July 22 the company unveiled Project Camellia, a four-building campus in Effingham County, Georgia, backed by at least $20 billion in private investment and drawing 3.2 gigawatts — enough for more than two million homes — under a 25-year supply agreement with Georgia Power, with electricity phased in from 2028 to 2032 and first operations targeted for 2028. OpenAI says it will pay the full cost of the electrical infrastructure so existing ratepayers are shielded, has offered up to one gigawatt of flexible demand response to steady the regional grid, and committed $80 million for local education, safety and health plus up to $71 million in Codex credits for Georgia students. Broader reporting puts full build-out spending above $30 billion, placing Camellia among the largest single AI facilities yet announced in the US. The detail worth watching is the structure, not the sticker: frontier labs are increasingly signing their own multi-decade utility deals and financing the substations themselves, taking direct control of power procurement because grid interconnection, not GPU supply, is now the binding constraint on frontier-scale compute.

sections.category: AI events to plan around: AMD's Advancing AI closes today, the Hot Chips early rate ends July 31, and the August security block is filling

bullets.body: The nearest catalyst is today and on the chip track: AMD's Advancing AI wraps up Thursday, July 23 with Lisa Su's keynote, livestreamed for anyone without a badge and covered above; the conference closes after today. The chip calendar's next fixed deadline is Friday, July 31 at 11:59 PM PDT, the Hot Chips early-registration cutoff, ahead of the conference itself August 23-25 at Stanford; the AI Infra Summit takes the Santa Clara Convention Center September 15-17, and Nvidia's GTC does not return to San Jose until March 15-18, 2027. The AI-security track clusters in early August: Black Hat USA runs August 1-6 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, with its AI Summit on Tuesday, August 4; DEF CON 34 follows August 6-9, its AI Village running capture-the-flag on attacks against agentic systems; and SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit takes Half Moon Bay on August 11-12. Booking further out: Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series adds Tokyo on September 15, London on October 8 and New York on October 21; SANS runs an AI Cybersecurity Summit November 2-3 in Arlington; and OWASP Global AppSec USA lands in San Francisco November 5-6, with training from November 2. On the developer and infrastructure track: Ai4 in Las Vegas August 4-6; the AI Tinkerers San Francisco meetup August 9; Ray Summit at the San Francisco Marriott Marquis August 24-26; the ACM AI Leadership Summit in Atlanta August 30 through September 2; OpenAI DevDay at Fort Mason September 29; The AI Conference at Pier 48 September 29 through October 1; the Runway AI Summit September 30; World Summit AI in Amsterdam October 7-8; PyTorch Conference in San Jose October 20-21; GitHub Universe October 28-29; AWS re:Invent November 30 through December 4; NeurIPS in December; IEEE-RAS Humanoids in Santa Clara December 7-9; and The AI Summit New York December 9-10. Practical sequencing: today's Advancing AI keynote is a browser tab rather than a trip across town, and the Hot Chips early rate has to be locked by July 31 before the August Las Vegas security block absorbs the calendar.
